issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig is a data race under async request handling
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this: _create_trtllm_generate_request flips lora_config.is_registered=True on a shared metadata object. Two concurrent FastAPI requests for the same LoRA can both observe False and either both ship weights or one skips weights before TRT-LLM has cached them. Registration is server-side identity-over-time state and must not live as a mutable field on a value passed by reference; move it behind a registry/lock or always send weights.

issues.description: lora_task_id is a global parse-time counter with no uniqueness or stability guarantee
issues.detail: task_id starts at 1 and increments across all repos and entries in iteration order during _parse_lora_configs. Across restarts, multiple repos, or reloads the same logical LoRA can land on a different task_id and collide with whatever TRT-LLM has cached. Derive the id deterministically from the name (or let the backend assign) and state the uniqueness scope.

issues.description: Bare except in _parse_lora_configs swallows all failures to None and prints traceback to stdout
issues.detail: The outer except Exception returns None for the whole repo, silently disabling LoRA, while print(traceback.format_exc()) dumps to stdout. Operators cannot distinguish 'no LoRA configured' from 'LoRA configured but broken'. Catch json.JSONDecodeError and OSError explicitly, let programming errors propagate, and route diagnostics through the logger.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs complects two backends, shadows lora_config_path, and mixes failure semantics
issues.detail: One branchy function handles vLLM model.json and TRT-LLM multi_lora.json, rebinds lora_config_path from a directory to a .npy file inside the TRT-LLM branch, and mixes ServerError re-raise with swallow-to-None. Split into _parse_vllm_loras and _parse_trtllm_loras returning the same value type, with a shared repo-resolution helper, and rename the inner path variable.

issues.description: Debug prints and unrelated traceback logging shipped in the hot path and across routers
issues.detail: print(f'backend: {backend}') fires per LoRA entry on every model load, and print(traceback.format_exc()) was added to chat/completions/embeddings routers plus the parser. These are unstructured debug crumbs with no log level, and the router changes are unrelated to the TRT-LLM LoRA feature. Delete the prints or route through the existing logger, and split unrelated changes into separate patches.

issues.description: Type annotations on _get_lora_config and _parse_lora_configs lie about return types and nullability
issues.detail: _get_lora_config is annotated -> TritonLoraConfig but returns None when lora_name is missing, and model_metadata.get(model_name) is dereferenced without a None check. _parse_lora_configs still claims List[tuple[str, str]] but returns List[TritonLoraConfig]. Fix both signatures to Optional[...] reflecting the post-refactor shape; the whole point was to stop pretending LoRA metadata is a string.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The refactor from lora_names to TritonLoraConfig is the right shape, but it ships with a real concurrency bug: is_registered is mutated on a shared config object from async FastAPI handlers, which all three reviewers flag as P0. Secondary problems cluster around identity and time: lora_task_id is a global parse-time counter with no stability or uniqueness scope, and the parser swallows all failures to None while printing tracebacks to stdout. The patch also bundles unrelated debug-logging changes across routers and leaves stray prints in the hot path. Fix the race, stabilize task_id, split the diff, and tighten the type signatures before merge.
